# Actual approval hierarchy

APPROVED STYLE DIRECTION, NOT APPROVED SPRITES: the file named “Pixel aesthetic reference — approved direction.png”, Drive ID 1s2xzQtWfZw_KJwf7xkuHA8cu1RqFs5kq, represents the user's chosen LOOK (small readable Kirby & the Amazing Mirror-era GBA pixel game), not approval to directly use Kirby-like characters, franchise-specific symbols, proposed names or a copied roster.

PROMISING BUT UNAPPROVED: current pixel-art gameplay studies, five quiet environment studies and E01 experimental proof. The owner specifically sought LESS visual stimulation, calmer backgrounds, readable platform geometry and character scale. Each promising image still requires selection/QA.

ARCHIVED/SUPERSEDED: earlier painterly, modern, 3D-ish and anime-like work belongs apart from current. Do not promote it.

REJECT OR EXCLUDE FROM ACTIVE ASSETS: large labeled poster/collage/asset-plan graphics, glossy/anime hero portraits, too-large characters versus platforms, inconsistent pixel grids, unreadable noisy environments, direct Kirby-like final character designs, or pseudo sprite sheets that are not separable working sprites.

Actual owner approval is the final gate on borderline choices; assistant aesthetic judgment is a filter, not a substitute for owner selection.

# Asset acceptance checklist

A. STYLE: visibly consistent with accepted GBA-era pixel-art aesthetic (but legally distinct original identities), simpler visual rhythms and restrained effects.

B. GAMEPLAY SCALE: side-on 2D geometry with walkable ground, clear collision planes, tiny expressive characters, distinct foreground and background. Not a fantasy poster/cinematic image.

C. ACTUAL REUSE: can become discrete sprites, layers, tiles, animations or a concrete gameplay interface rather than a giant uneditable collage.

D. TECHNICAL QUALITY: consistent grid and tile seams; consistent palette/pixel density; reliable transparent layers for real production assets; legible native pixel-size silhouettes.

E. CONTENT: no invented approved roster, forced lore, giant narrative labels, baked text in game art, generic "epic" bombast, or copyright-confusing recognizably Kirby-owned designs.

F. REVIEW: mark exact asset APPROVED, CANDIDATE, EXPERIMENTAL, SUPERSEDED, or REJECTED. User-approved final assets only go into an explicitly approved/production folder; candidates may remain in a named exploration folder.

G. NO ASSUMED GENERATION: a design document naming a sprite or environment does NOT mean that art exists. The 66-deliverable art backlog is planned, not 66 files already created.

# Design coverage / integration quality

Current docs record central premise, three NPC modes, NO NPC AI, minimal dialogue, active-world exploration, unlockable party, acquired power loss, physical successful signals before reinforcements, good-guy mode 2 reversible versus mode 3 cooldown, persistent cross-level chase and faction conflicts, enemy outpost alarms, Hall of Legends, detailed playable level ideas, exploration percentages / hidden mystery components, and Cantina / shared party / infinite Smash brawl / shortcut door lockout / completion override with guards following inside.

The design still uses append-only owner corrections, so historical paragraphs contradict newer decisions. A truly fully maintained canonical spec would rewrite each pertinent section and keep change history separated. Proposals must not be promoted to confirmed canonical levels, final mechanics, or finished assets.

# Immediate outcome of this audit

NO new PNGs were imported into the active Drive assets. This is intentional: the user explicitly prefers correctness and quality over completeness-by-volume. The confirmed aesthetic reference is already in Drive. Existing superseded art remains segregated; no originals were deleted.

Recommendation: continue creating/testing one modular gameplay-sized pixel asset at a time, comparing against the approved reference and reviewing with the owner before promoting it.
